A request from a program to the kernel for a service

Two threads each hold a lock and wait for the lock held by the other thread
A thread is never scheduled because other threads always have priority
Several threads finish their work at exactly the same clock tick

A slice based on its priority
A slice based on its burst

q: A low-priority process never getting the CPU is called:

A boolean flag that the scheduler sets when a process becomes ready to run
A hardware register that stores the address of the current instruction
A table that maps each virtual page of a process to a physical frame

r: NSCT area: Operating Systems, sub-area: Concurrency and synchronization. Further reading: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts (synchronization tools).

Up to N threads at a time to hold it
Any thread to release it at any time
Readers to share it while writers wait

r: NSCT area: Operating Systems, sub-area: Deadlocks. Further reading: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts (deadlocks).

A fast cache of recent page table entries
A queue of pages waiting to be swapped
A buffer of disk blocks read recently

A static public IP address for every device

Automated scanning that lists missing software patches
Reviewing security policies without touching any systems
Monitoring live network traffic for signs of an intrusion
